purpose: Manual package screening before optimization; three identical fixed wrist motors and independent choices only at J1, J2 and J3.

policy.speed: At 30:1, the current targets need 900 motor rpm for J1-J3 and 1500 rpm for J4-J6. Every selectable motor exceeds these speeds.
policy.priorities: Adequate torque/speed first, retaining useful driver-current, body-length and net-mass tradeoffs. Diameter is secondary but its real envelope remains in the model. The lower-listed-current 36 V J2 choices are retained despite their larger packages; actual motor heating is unverified.
policy.rated_power: Rated mechanical watts approximately equal rated torque times rated angular speed. Lower rated rpm/watts alone do not establish lower operating consumption, loss or mass. Efficiency maps are unavailable.
policy.voltage: Keep one 36 V BSA62 winding as the mechanical representative of its otherwise equal 24 V package. This does not establish equal electrical losses or prescribe a common supply bus.
policy.wrist: The user requested roughly the 0.066 Nm class, interpreted from the lower-torque/size request. Use three copies of verified 0.063 Nm BSB41. It is a compact sizing candidate, not a claim that the faster motion suite passes.
policy.unknowns: No shipping weight is substituted for net motor mass. Missing rotor inertia, transient motor torque and loss maps stay unpublished; the existing simulation upper-bound policy is recorded separately.
policy.coverage: This is an explicitly reduced study, not a proof that rejected tradeoffs can never be optimal. Original supplier records and prior run snapshots are retained. Enumerate the same shortlisted hardware tuples in each layout; continuous geometry remains a finite optimization.

SO_42BLR43-24-01.reason: 250 g and 43 mm, but the fresh main product page specifies preorder MOQ 30. Not a single-motor purchase candidate; only 12 g lighter and 2 mm longer than BSB41.

SO_42BLS40-24-01.reason: Compact 39.2 mm current body, but net motor mass is absent from checked HTML/PDF. The 300 g shipping weight cannot establish a lighter motor.

SO_42BLS60-24-01.reason: No published net motor mass in the retained source; cannot import shipping mass or make a weight comparison.

SO_42BSA46-24-01.reason: Useful 0.08 Nm step-up alternative: 46 mm, 280 g. Current 0.063 Nm common-wrist preference chooses BSB41, which is 5 mm shorter and 18 g lighter. Reserve is not a claim that its extra torque is useless.

SO_42BSA62-24-01.reason: Same modeled 0.16 Nm, 3000 rpm, 62 mm and 430 g package as the retained 36 V winding. Preserve the electrical variant in research; do not spend duplicate mechanical search evaluations.

SO_42BSA62-36-01.reason: Retain the lighter 0.16 Nm package: 62 mm, 430 g, 3000 rpm, 50 W rated. Useful length/mass tradeoff against the shorter 57 mm models.

SO_42BSA78-24-01.reason: 0.24 Nm is only 0.01 Nm above BLR50, but its 78 mm body is 28.9 mm longer and its 580 g mass is 80 g higher. Manual length/mass tradeoff exclusion, not strict torque dominance.

SO_42BSA78-48-01.reason: 48 V winding is outside the current 24/36 V study; the long/heavy package is also not preferred.

SO_42BSB41-24-01.reason: Fixed common wrist model: 0.063 Nm, 3000 rpm, 20 W rated, 41 mm, verified 262 g, USD 13.90. Fits the existing 110 mm wrist. Fast-load adequacy is still a simulation question.

SO_42BSB61-24-01.reason: 0.125 Nm, 61 mm and 438 g. BSA62 provides 0.16 Nm with less mass and only 1 mm more length; little useful package benefit for this shortlist.

SO_42BSB61-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study and the BSB61 package is not preferred.

SO_42BSB81-24-01.reason: BLR50 provides more torque (0.23 versus 0.19 Nm), 31.9 mm less length and 116 g less mass at sufficient speed.

SO_42BSB81-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study and the long/heavy BSB81 package is not preferred.

SO_42BYA43-24-01.reason: Light 200 g motor, but 0.04 Nm gives only 1.2 Nm ideal output at 30:1, below the recalled wrist demand and recorded J5 gravity loads. Not selected as the common J4-J6 model.

SO_42BYA51-24-01.reason: Useful 0.08 Nm step-up option: 51 mm, 260 g. It saves only 2 g versus the chosen BSB41 while adding 10 mm length. Retain in research for a wrist torque upgrade if needed.

SO_42BYA73-24-01.reason: At 0.16 Nm, it saves only 10 g versus BSA62 but adds 11 mm body length. Manual exclusion under the user's axial-length priority; its slimmer diameter remains documented.

SO_57BLR50-24-01.reason: Compact stronger option: 0.23 Nm, 3500 rpm, 49.1 mm, 500 g. More torque, less length and less mass than the 0.19/0.20 Nm alternatives at all required speeds.

SO_57BLR50-36-01.reason: Same 49.1 mm, 500 g package as the 24 V BLR50, but only 0.11 Nm at 4000 rpm. Higher nominal voltage does not make it a stronger or lighter choice.

SO_57BLR70-24-02.reason: Strongest retained motor: 0.47 Nm, 3500 rpm, 74 mm, 650 g. J2 candidate and stronger J1/J3 alternatives. Nominal power is 172 W, not an assumed operating draw.

SO_57BLR70-36-01.reason: BLR50-24 supplies slightly more torque (0.23 versus 0.22 Nm), saves 20 mm length and 150 g; both exceed required speed.

SO_57BLY54-24-01.reason: Retain the short lightweight 0.16 Nm alternative: 53.5 mm, 450 g. It is 20 g lighter than the same-length 3000 rpm BYA54 despite its 4000 rpm/67 W rating; operating efficiency is unknown.

SO_57BSA58-24-01.reason: BLR50 supplies 0.23 versus 0.20 Nm, saves 8.9 mm length and 100 g, and meets all target speeds. Lower nameplate watts are not evidence of lower consumption.

SO_57BSA79-36-01.reason: BLR70 supplies 0.47 versus 0.40 Nm, saves 5 mm length and 280 g, and meets all target speeds.

SO_57BYA54-24-01.reason: Retain the shorter 3000 rpm 0.16 Nm package: 53.5 mm, 470 g, 50 W rated. Compare its 20 g mass penalty with the same-size 4000 rpm BLY54 rather than assuming an efficiency advantage.

SO_57BYA74-36-01.reason: BLR70 supplies more torque (0.47 versus 0.32 Nm) and saves 110 g for only 0.5 mm extra body length. Manual torque/mass tradeoff exclusion.

SO_57BYA94-36-01.reason: 36 V J2 alternative: 0.45 Nm, 3000 rpm, 5.4 A listed, 93.5 mm round body, 1030 g, USD 36.74. Lower listed current than 24 V BLR70 trades against 19.5 mm extra length and 380 g extra mass; current convention and motor heating remain unverified.

SO_57BSD96-36-01.reason: 36 V J2 alternative: 0.45 Nm, 3000 rpm, 5.4 A listed, 96 mm square body, 810 g, USD 24.83. It is 220 g lighter than BYA94 but 2.5 mm longer and has a larger square bounding envelope. No efficiency or temperature advantage is inferred from amperes alone.

SO_57BYA94-48-01.reason: 48 V winding outside the current study; not needed for this manually reduced motor palette.
